text.en:
Every year Gauri's family travelled to a river bank to bathe and pray. Thousands of other families gathered there too.
They carried food and sang songs along the way.
"This is a journey to a sacred place," said her grandmother. "We call it a pilgrimage."

People in India regard many rivers, mountains, forests, trees and places as sacred. Rivers such as the Ganga, Kaveri, Godavari and Yamuna, mountains such as the Himalayas and Kailash, and many temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras and other shrines are visited by devotees.
A journey to a holy place is called a pilgrimage. Pilgrims travel on foot, by bullock cart or by train. Many fairs and festivals are held at sacred places, such as the Kumbh Mela, which draws crowds in millions.
Sacred geography links people with nature and with each other. It brings communities together, supports local trade and the economy, and asks us to protect these places and keep them clean.
In India many rivers, mountains and trees are regarded as sacred.
A journey to a holy place is called a pilgrimage.
Large fairs such as the Kumbh Mela gather millions of people.
We must keep sacred places clean and protect them.

problem.en: How does a pilgrimage help the people of the place that is visited?

text.en: Pilgrims need food, shelter and goods.
Shopkeepers, guides and boatmen earn from the visitors.
So pilgrimage supports the local economy and brings people together.

why.en: It also needs care of the place.

prompt.en: A friend throws plastic into a sacred river. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Sacred rivers must be kept clean and respected.
Plastic harms the river and the people who depend on it.

points.en: Rivers, mountains and places are sacred to many people.
A journey to a holy place is a pilgrimage.
We must protect and keep sacred places clean.
